 Politics & Policy Trump lands in China for historic meeting with Xi, Putin
 Published Wed, Nov 18 2026 3:45 AM EST Updated 5 Min Ago Anniek Bao @in/anniek-bao-460a48107/ @anniekbyx Natalie Feary WATCH LIVE Key Points President Donald Trump has arrived in Shenzhen for the APEC summit ahead of historic trilateral talks Thursday with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
 The Trump-Xi-Putin meeting is expected to focus on the Iran war, Russia’s war in Ukraine and broader strategic stability, though expectations for a concrete outcome are low.
 Xi opened the summit by calling for free trade, greater cooperation on artificial intelligence and stronger multilateral ties, while Putin argued that sanctions on Russia have backfired.

 Trump is in China for the APEC summit, which President Xi opened with calls for free trade and greater cooperation around artificial intelligence. 
 He said: "We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition."
 Putin has also addressed the summit , saying sanctions imposed on Russia have backfired and strengthened his nation.
 US President Donald Trump (R) is greeted by China's President Xi Jinping as he arrives at Shenzhen Baoan International Airport to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on November 18, 2026. (Photo by Mandel NGAN / POOL / AFP via Getty Images) Mandel Ngan | Afp | Getty Images The much-anticipated meeting between the three world leaders is set to take place on Thursday, with discussions expected to center on the Iran war and Russia's war in Ukraine. 
 Though expectations for any concrete outcome are low, Trump, Xi and Putin are expected to hold in-depth discussions on issues crucial for world peace and strategic stability, a spokesperson for China's foreign ministry said Monday.
 North Korean leader Kim Jong-Un could attend the summit, which is a forum of 21 APEC member economies.
 Trump flew in from Manila, Philippines, where he started a three-day visit to Asia and met key regional allies including Japan, India and Australia. 
 US President Donald Trump stands at the top of the stairs of Air Force One as he arrives at Shenzhen Baoan International Airport to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on November 18, 2026. (Photo by Mandel NGAN / POOL / AFP via Getty Images) Mandel Ngan | Afp | Getty Images The APEC host city Shenzhen has been dubbed one of China's "Silicon Valleys" and has been a major hub for China's internet and artificial intelligence companies. 
 The summit offers an opportunity for Beijing to present itself as a steward of multilateralism against what it terms "unilateralism and protectionism," with trade, artificial intelligence, and the Middle East expected to dominate the meeting's agenda. 
 Xi held several bilateral meetings with leaders on the sidelines Wednesday, including South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, with whom he discussed trade and commerce. Seoul's readout of the meeting also said the pair discussed peace on the Korean Peninsula, but this was omitted from Beijing's record of the talks.

Putin was received with an official welcoming ceremony outside Great Hall of the People, where Xi greeted him, before the two sit for talks. (Photo by Kremlin Press Service/Anadolu via Getty Images) Anadolu | Anadolu | Getty Images The Chinese leader also met Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Vietnamese President To Lam earlier in the week.
 Xi met with Putin earlier Wednesday, before Trump's arrival. The Chinese president called for greater cooperation between the two countries and spoke of providing a more stable and predictable business environment, according to Chinese state media, while promoting a "multipolar world and democratization of international relations."
 Putin said Russia was looking to expand cooperation in trade, energy and education. The reports did not address Russia's war in Ukraine or the Iran war.
 Trump will also hold bilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, amid hopes the pair can secure a lasting trade truce beyond January 2027. The meeting comes as the U.S. seeks to curb exports of artificial intelligence chips and amid concerns that Nvidia chips may have been diverted to China.
